name: Carta de Nacionalización

requirements.blocker_text: Must hold Residencia Definitiva (permanent residence) at the time of application.
More than 5 years of residence in Chile (continuity requirement removed by Law 20.888, effective 8 January 2016).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate more than 5 years of residence in Chile.

requirements.blocker_text: Minimum age 18 (reduced from 21 by Law 20.888); children of foreigners may apply from age 14 with parental authorization.

requirement_groups.name: Minor child of a recognised refugee

requirements.blocker_text: A child under 18 with at least one parent holding recognised refugee status may naturalise without meeting the standard residence/age requirements.

evidence_required.document: Tax documentation confirming no outstanding debt

sources.title: Carey y Cía. (Chilean law firm) -- summary of Law 20.888 (effective 8 January 2016) amending naturalisation requirements: more than 5 years' residence (continuity requirement removed), minimum age reduced from 21 to 18 (14 for children of foreigners with parental authorization), and a fast-track for minor children of recognised refugees

serviciomigraciones.cl (SERMIG) -- Carta de Nacionalización: available to Residencia Definitiva holders, Residencia Definitiva holders with family ties to a Chilean citizen, and children of naturalised refugees

STATUS: DRAFT -- the eligibility STRUCTURE (who may apply) is tier-1 (SERMIG's own citizenship page), but the specific residence-year figure (5 years), the minimum-age figures, and the 2016 legislative history all come from a tier-3 law firm summary rather than a fetched government or gazette text of Law 20.888 itself -- every hard requirement in this file traces to that tier-3 source, so the file is held to draft per this dataset's validator rule (published requires tier-1 sourcing on every hard requirement) despite the tier-1 structural corroboration. Flagged for future re-verification against a primary legal text (Law 20.888 itself, or BCN's ley chile database). dual_citizenship_allowed is left NULL rather than asserted -- no source fetched in this pass directly confirmed Chile's current dual-citizenship policy for naturalising foreigners, and it is flagged as unconfirmed rather than stated from unaided recall. STRUCTURAL FINDING: Chile's family-tie discount applies at the RESIDENCIA DEFINITIVA stage (12-month reduced wait, see cl_permanent_residence.json), not as a separate marriage-citizenship application at THIS stage -- no distinct 'citizenship by marriage' route exists once a person already holds Residencia Definitiva; the 5-year/18-year-old naturalisation conditions apply uniformly regardless of how PR was obtained. This is disclosed explicitly rather than building a duplicate marriage-citizenship file that doesn't reflect Chile's actual process.
